key_insight: Transformer-based neural quantum states can generalize at inference time under in-context learning, with pointwise error shrinking as in-context examples and Transformer depth increase.
engineering_relevance: This provides a scaling law for designing quantum machine-learning models, suggesting depth grows only linearly with system size while still supporting generalization guarantees.
method: Derive a rigorous MSE generalization bound for in-context inference.
Show error decreases inversely with the number of in-context examples and Transformer depth.
Extend the analysis from point predictions to full quantum states via rank-one density operators under physical constraints.
evidence_signal: The paper reports numerical simulations that corroborate the theoretical MSE-based generalization analysis across continuous and discrete settings.
watch_item: The guarantees are theoretical and depend on physical/modeling assumptions, so practical performance may differ if the training distribution or constraints are violated.
paper_title: Generalization of Transformer-Based Neural Quantum States via In-Context Learning
